properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 declares SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations that ship in the mainnet-fork/get_wsol and tmp node builds (transitive dep of the Serum/Ethereum-style tooling); no direct first-party call site, but the algorithms are available in the shipped node_modules — this IS the dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 npm package (^4.0.2, Ethereum-style ECDSA/signing on secp256k1) ships in the node_modules of 5 workspace projects (mainnet-fork, mainnet-fork/get_wsol, onchain-data, program, tmp) as a transitive dependency of Serum/Ethereum-style tooling; no first-party call site seen in the project's TS code, but the algorithm is available in the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 signatures in the Rust arbitrage client: Solana transactions are Ed25519-signed, and ed25519-dalek@1.0.1 is locked in client/Cargo.lock (pulled by the solana-sdk stack). The client also declares Ed25519 in its npm lockfile. Changeable here — upgrade path is ML-DSA-65 per FIPS 204.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 provides ECDSA (secp256k1/secp256r1) in the mainnet-fork/get_wsol build; no first-party call site, but the algorithm ships with the build — available in the shipped library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek@3.2.1 in the Rust client's dependency tree — the Curve25519 arithmetic layer under ed25519-dalek used for Solana transaction signing. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 also provides ECDH key agreement in the same shipped node_modules; same package as the ECDSA object (ALG-710f61f0) — classical curve primitives available in the build, no first-party call site seen.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: keccak@3.0.1 (Ethereum-flavoured Keccak/SHA-3) ships in the mainnet-fork node build as a transitive dep of the Serum/Ethereum tooling; no first-party call site seen, but the algorithm is available in the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 available in two stacks: the Rust pbkdf2 crate 0.4.0 (client/Cargo.lock — typical of solana-sdk's BIP39 mnemonic→seed derivation path) and a JS pbkdf2 package in tmp/yarn.lock. No first-party call site with explicit parameters seen; the algorithm ships in both builds.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: First-party SHA-256 (sha2 crate): both hashers derive the Anchor 8-byte method discriminator from "global:swap" (Sha256::new() → update("global:swap") → finalize → first 8 bytes) to build Aldrin DEX v1/v2 swap CPI instructions. Grover only square-roots preimage resistance; not urgent. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC (hmac crate 0.8.1) available in the Rust client build — typically pulled in by the bip39/pbkdf2 seed-derivation stack of solana-sdk; no first-party call site seen, but the MAC ships with the binary.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2@0.10.2 locked in client/Cargo.lock — SHA-256 hashing in the Rust client (Solana pool/program id derivation and swap-program hashing also use SHA-256 in the on-chain program sources).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 1.3.1 available in the Rust client build (solana-sdk uses blake3 for program-hash/transaction hashing); no first-party call site seen, but the algorithm ships with the binary. BLAKE3 has comfortable security margins against Grover.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM from ring@0.16.20 in the client's dependency tree — the AEAD protecting the rustls TLS sessions the client opens to Solana RPC endpoints. Symmetric primitive; the PQ concern for these sessions is the X25519 key exchange, not the AEAD.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@1.0.3 is what @solana/web3.js uses underneath Keypair (Ed25519 sign/verify) — it also ships XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox; available in the shipped node_modules even though first-party code only exercises the Ed25519 path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls 0.20.4 is the TLS provider in the Rust client's dependency tree (via solana-client/reqwest): TLS 1.3-capable but 0.20.x negotiates only classical key exchange (X25519/P-256/finite-field DHE via ring) — no post-quantum KEM groups. Harvestable RPC traffic to Solana nodes until the provider is upgraded and hybrid groups are offered.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.16.20 is the crypto provider behind rustls 0.20 and supplies the classical primitives (X25519, P-256, AES-GCM, SHA-2, Ed25519) in the Rust client build; available in the shipped binary.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ed25519-dalek@1.0.1 locked in client/Cargo.lock — the Ed25519 implementation the Rust client uses for Solana transaction signing and pubkey handling. Same logical dependency as the Ed25519 algorithm entry ALG-683d5cd2, recorded at library level.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.11 declared in tmp/yarn.lock — SHA-256/SHA-512 hashing for the TypeScript tooling that lives in tmp/. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: blake3@1.3.1 locked in client/Cargo.lock — BLAKE3 hashing in the client's dependency tree (solana-sdk hashes program accounts and instructions with BLAKE3). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 in mainnet-fork/get_wsol/package-lock.json — the package object for the ECDSA (ALG-710f61f0) and ECDH (ALG-c9ffc8a8) algorithm objects drawn from the same shipped library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hmac@0.8.1 locked in client/Cargo.lock — HMAC in the Rust client's dependency tree (part of the solana-sdk crypto stack). Changeable here.
